subject.title: Org owners cannot roll back latest after accidental higher-version skill publish

question: Should organization publisher owners be able to repoint `latest` to any existing eligible version, or should recovery be limited to an explicit replacement-and-delete workflow?
rationale: Both approaches alter the public package-version contract and need an explicit rule for eligibility, auditing, and whether a lower semver may become `latest`.

options.title: Add audited tag rollback
options.body: Authorize publisher owners/admins to point `latest` at an existing public, security-eligible version and retain the accidental version in history.

options.title: Use replacement-only recovery
options.body: Keep tags monotonic and add a narrowly authorized workflow that supplies an explicit replacement before deleting the current latest.

recommendation.title: Add audited tag rollback
recommendation.body: Authorize publisher owners/admins to point `latest` at an existing public, security-eligible version and retain the accidental version in history.

likelyOwner.reason: A history-backed individual owner could not be resolved in the read-only environment; the decision belongs with the publisher/version contract owner.
